Formulas.Description: Berths for whole vessels. The one thing a cargo hold cannot carry: a ship arrives and leaves under its own power, so a dock answers HOW MANY and HOW BIG rather than how much fits. Split the same tonnage into fewer wide berths or many narrow ones - a tender is one big door, a carrier is several small ones, and each door costs structure.

Properties.Name: Berth Tonnage
Properties.DescriptionFormula: 'Total docked hull mass the bay supports. This is the budget every berth is carved out of.'

Properties.Name: Berths
Properties.DescriptionFormula: 'How many vessels dock at once. The SAME total tonnage split more ways, so each door gets narrower - and every extra door costs structure and deck crew.'

Properties.Name: Max Hull Mass
Properties.DescriptionFormula: 'The largest SINGLE vessel that fits through a door. Emergent: total tonnage divided by the number of berths. Two small bays never combine into one big one.'
